Tensor Analysis – Practical 4 Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 4.1 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + i2 − i3, e2 = i1 + i2, e3 = i1 − i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (2, 0, −1). (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (2, 0, −1). 4.2 [See lecture] Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + 2i2 + 4i3, e2 = i2, e3 = i1 + 2i2 + 5i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (1, 1, 1). (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector joining the origin to the point (1, 1, 1). 4.3 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the a new coordinate system K′ with basis vectors e1 = i1 + 2i2, e2 = 2i1 + 2i2 + 4i3, e3 = 2i3. (1) Find a basis e1, e2, e3 dual to e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant components of the vector C = 2i2 + 2i3. (3) Find the contravariant components of the vector C = 2i2 + 2i3. 1

2 4.4 Given an orthogonal coordinate system K with orthonormal basis i1, i2, i3, consider the vector B with components B = i1 + 3i2. Let K be a new coordinate system with basis vectors e ′ 1 = i1, e ′ 2 = i1 − i2, e ′ 3 = i1 + i2 + i3. (1) Work out the expansion coefficients L1 i′, L2 i′, L3 i′ for each i = 1, 2, 3. (2) Compute the covariant components B′ i of B in the coordinate system K′. (3) Find a basis dual to e′ 1, e′ 2, e′ 3. (4) Compute the contravariant components B′i of B in the coordinate system K′. (5) Let gik = e′i ·e′k. Compute these gik for all i, k = 1, 2, 3. (It might be more convenient to write your answers as the entries of a matrix.) (6) Using your answers to parts (2) and (5), work out the contravariant components B′i of B in K′ in another way. 4.5 [Question from Final Exam 23-24] In this question, denote by K the Cartesian coordinate system with vector basis i1, i2, i3, the standard orthonormal basis of R3. Denote by K′ the coordinate system with vector basis e1, e2, e3 given by e1 = 2i1 + i3 e2 = i2 e3 = i1 − i2 + i3. (1) Find the dual basis e1, e2, e3. (2) Find the covariant and contravariant components of the vector V = 3i1 − 2i2 + i3 with respect to the bases e1, e2, e3 and e1, e2, e3. 4.6 Consider dual bases e1, e2, e3 and e1, e2, e3, and denote V = e1 · (e2 × e3), and V ′ = e 1 · (e 2 × e 3). Show, using the vector triple product formula, that V ′ = 1/V . 4.7 [See lecture] Express the scalar triple product (A × B) · C in terms of the covariant and contravariant components of the vectors A, B and C, with respect to dual bases. You may use the equalities (1) A × B = (AjBk − AkBj)V = 1 V (AjBk − AkBj).
